who: Aristotle · as told by Diogenes Laertius, Lives V.18, tr. R. D. Hicks, 1925
quote: The roots of education... are bitter, but the fruit is sweet.
meaning: Learning tastes bitter at the start. Later it gives sweet fruit.

who: ‘Standing in the snow at Cheng's gate’ · History of Song, juan 428, tr. from Chinese
quote: Two students found their teacher Cheng Yi sitting with his eyes closed. They stood by him and waited. When he woke, the snow outside the door was a foot deep.
meaning: They waited quietly for their teacher while a foot of snow fell outside.

who: Vidura, the wise counsellor · Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva 40, tr. K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96
quote: Votaries of pleasure must give up knowledge, and votaries of knowledge must give up pleasure.
meaning: You cannot have all the comfort and all the learning. To learn, give up some comfort.

who: Three Character Classic, 13th century · tr. Herbert A. Giles, 1900
quote: ...one who put fireflies in a bag, and again another who used the white glare from snow. Although their families were poor, these men studied unceasingly.
meaning: No money for lamp oil? One boy read by fireflies, another by snow light.

who: Cleanthes · as told by Diogenes Laertius, Lives VII.168-174, tr. R. D. Hicks, 1925
quote: Cleanthes drew water in gardens by night so he could study with Zeno by day. Too poor for paper, he wrote the lectures on oyster-shells and ox bones.
meaning: He worked at night to learn by day. Later he took his teacher's place.

who: Antisthenes · Diogenes Laertius, Lives VI.2, tr. R. D. Hicks, 1925
quote: Already a teacher, Antisthenes became a pupil of Socrates. He ‘every day would tramp the five miles to Athens in order to hear Socrates.’
meaning: He became a student again, and walked about 8 km to class every day.

who: Mikhail Lomonosov · letter of 10 May 1753, tr. from Russian
quote: At 19, fisherman's son Mikhail Lomonosov walked to Moscow to study. He lived on bread and kvass: ‘Thus I lived five years, and did not give up learning.’
meaning: Five poor years on bread and kvass, a cheap drink. He kept studying.

quote: Often I sat up in my room reading the greatest part of the night, when the book was borrowed in the evening and to be returned early in the morning...
meaning: He read most of the night, because the borrowed book had to go back by morning.

who: Fukuzawa Yukichi, student in Osaka, 1850s · Autobiography, tr. Eiichi Kiyooka, 1934
quote: Fukuzawa looked for his pillow: ‘I realized suddenly that I had not used one for the whole year... I had been studying without regard to day or night...’
meaning: He studied day and night for a whole year and never once slept on a pillow.

who: T. Krishnamacharya · as told by his son T. K. V. Desikachar, The Heart of Yoga, 1995
quote: As his son tells it, in 1916 Krishnamacharya went to the Himalayas to find his teacher, Ramamohan Brahmachari, and stayed more than seven years.
meaning: He became Pattabhi Jois's teacher. Our Ashtanga line goes back to this search.
